## Why This Is Asked
Tests end-to-end security for ML artifacts, combining signing attestations, GitOps, and runtime policy in Kubernetes.

## Key Concepts
- Sigstore Cosign sign-blob attest and verify-blob
- Model provenance and SBOM
- GitOps with Argo CD
- Admission policies: OPA Gatekeeper or Kyverno

## Code Example
```bash
# Sign a model blob and create an attestation
cosign sign-blob -key cosign.key models/model-v1.bin
cosign attest -key cosign.key --predicate predicate.json models/model-v1.bin
cosign verify-blob -key cosign.pub models/model-v1.bin
```

```yaml
# Kyverno policy requiring attestation before deployment
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-model-attestation
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: attested-model-artifact
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: [Deployment]
    validate:
      message: Attestation required for model artifact
      pattern:
        metadata.annotations.cosign_attested: "true"
```

```rego
package kubernetes.admission

deny[{"msg": msg}] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Deployment"
  not input.request.object.metadata.annotations["cosign_attested"] == "true"
  msg = "Model artifact must be attested with cosign before deployment"
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle key rotation and revocation?
- How would you test end-to-end in CI/CD and cluster?

```yaml
# Kyverno policy example (high level)
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-signed-images

      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment"]
```

## Why This Is Asked

Tests understanding of Helm templating and basic policy checks in CI for secure defaults, plus ability to craft a simple gate that a junior engineer can implement.

## Key Concepts

- Helm templating and values.yaml
- YAML validation with yq
- Kubernetes securityContext basics
- Image tag policy and registry scoping
- CI gate design and test manifests

## Code Example

```yaml
# .github/workflows/helm-gate.yml
name: Helm gate
on: push
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - uses: azure/setup-helm@v1
      - name: Render charts
        run: helm template mychart charts/mychart > /tmp/rendered.yaml
      - name: Validate images
        run: |
          if ! yq e '.items[].spec.template.spec.containers[].image' /tmp/rendered.yaml | grep -q registry.example.com/secure/; then echo image origin invalid; exit 1; fi
```

```yaml
# failing Deployment manifest
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: myservice
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: registry.example.com/secure/myservice:latest
          # missing securityContext and resources
```

```yaml
# passing Deployment manifest
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: myservice
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: registry.example.com/secure/myservice:v1.2.3
          securityContext:
            runAsNonRoot: true
            runAsUser: 1000
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 100m
              memory: 128Mi
            limits:
              cpu: 200m
              memory: 256Mi
```

- How would you extend to multi-container pods?
- How would you adapt for multiple charts in a single repo?

## Why This Is Asked
Assesses practical CI gating, SBOM generation, and license compliance in a mono-repo.

- SBOM generation with Syft
- SPDX license checks and whitelisting
- Per-service CI gates in a mono-repo

## Code Example
```yaml
name: SBOM and License Gate
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Build image
        run: |
          echo "build service image"
      - name: Generate SBOM
        run: |
          syft image:myorg/service:sha -o json > sbom.json
      - name: Upload SBOM
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
        with:
          name: sbom.json
          path: sbom.json
      - name: License check
        run: |
          if on_disallowed_license; then exit 1; fi
```

- How would you auto-fix or report to maintainers?

```yaml
# minimal GitHub Actions workflow (illustrative)
name: ci
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  verify-sign:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

        run: cosign verify --key infra/cosign.pub $IMAGE
      - name: sign image
        run: cosign sign --key infra/cosign.pub $IMAGE
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to translate security requirements into policy-as-code, enforce across workload types, and validate in CI. It also probes tool choice (Kyverno vs OPA Gatekeeper), namespace scoping, and test design.

## Key Concepts
- Runtime security posture with securityContext fields
- Policy engines: Kyverno, OPA Gatekeeper
- Resource types: Deployments, StatefulSets, DaemonSets
- Local and CI validation strategies

## Code Example
```yaml
# Kyverno cluster policy example
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: enforce-runtime-hardening
spec:
  rules:
  - name: require-secure-pod
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ['Deployment','StatefulSet','DaemonSet']
    validate:
      message: 'Containers must be non-root, readOnlyRootFilesystem, and drop ALL capabilities'
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - name: '*'
                securityContext:
                  runAsNonRoot: true
                  runAsUser: 1000
                  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
                  allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
                  capabilities:
                    drop: ['ALL']
```

```yaml
# Failing manifest example (violates rules)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: fail-noncompliant
spec:
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: fail
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: example/app:latest
        securityContext:
          runAsUser: 0
          privileged: true
          capabilities:
            add: ['NET_ADMIN']
      volumes:
      - name: data
        hostPath:
          path: /data
```

```yaml
# Passing manifest example
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: compliant
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: example/app:1.2.3
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 1000
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          capabilities:
            drop: ['ALL']
```

- Verification steps: locally run kyverno test, simulate with kubectl apply and audit via kyverno CLI; CI gate runs kyverno/opa checks on PR.

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle exceptions per-namespace or per-tenant?
- How would you measure false positives in CI across multiple clusters?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to enforce cross-cloud data provenance and model lineage for ML workloads; ensures reproducibility and auditing of deployments.

## Key Concepts
- Policy-as-code with Kyverno/OPA Gatekeeper
- Image digests, internal registries, provenance annotations
- MLflow tracking integration and run_id propagation
- Local and CI validation strategies

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: enforce-ml-provenance
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Fail
  rules:
  - name: require-provenance-annotations
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Deployment
    validate:
      message: 'Missing provenance annotations: model_version, dataset_hash, training_run_id'
      pattern:
        metadata:
          annotations:
            model_version: '*'
            dataset_hash: '*'
            training_run_id: '*'
  - name: require-image-digest
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Deployment
    validate:
      message: 'Container image must include a digest'
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - image: '*@*'
```

```yaml
# Failing Deployment (no provenance)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: ml-inference-fail
  annotations:
    model_version: v1
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: ml
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: predictor
        image: registry.internal/ml/predictor:latest
```

```yaml
# Passing Deployment (with provenance and digest)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: ml-inference-pass
  annotations:
    model_version: v1.2.3
    dataset_hash: sha256:abcdef1234567890
    training_run_id: tr-789
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: ml
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: predictor
        image: registry.internal/ml/predictor@sha256:12345abcdef
```

- conftest with YAML schemas for Kubernetes objects

## CI Verification
- Run policy gate in CI on pull requests; ensure failing manifests block merges and passing manifests are allowed.

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design a reject-by-default policy for hostPath usage, a common attack surface, and to describe how to maintain a dynamic allowlist in production.

## Key Concepts
- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- hostPath volumes and host filesystem access risk
- dynamic allowlist via a ConfigMap and a small controller to sync data
- CI validation (dry-run, gatekeeper admissions) and runtime validation

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: HostPathPolicy
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: HostPathConstraint
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package hostpathpolicy
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
        some i in input.review.object.spec.volumes
        input.review.object.spec.volumes[i].hostPath
        not data.hostpath_allowlist.namespaces[_]
        msg := "hostPath volumes are forbidden unless in allowlist"
      }
```

```yaml
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: HostPathConstraint
metadata:
  name: hostpath-deny
spec:
  match:
    kinds:
    - apiGroups: ["v1"]
      kinds: ["Pod"]
```

Compliant manifest (no hostPath):
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: compliant-pod
  namespace: default
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx:1.23
```

Noncompliant manifest (hostPath present):
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: noncompliant-pod
  namespace: default
spec:
  volumes:
  - name: data
    hostPath:
      path: /var/lib/data
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx:1.23
    volumeMounts:
    - mountPath: /data
      name: data
```

CI/runtime validation plan: run Gatekeeper admission checks on PRs, simulate allowed namespaces via the ConfigMap sync, and perform a runtime audit post-deploy using a test pod to verify policy enforcement.

## Why This Is Asked
- Evaluates practical policy design for observability in cloud-native platforms
- Tests knowledge of admission control, Kyverno policies, and CI integration

## Key Concepts
- OpenTelemetry instrumentation methods (sidecars vs. environment variables)
- Kyverno policy patterns and validation rules
- CI verification of policy enforcement and runtime tracing

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-otel-tracing
spec:
 rules:
 - name: require-otel-annotation
   match:
     resources:
       kinds: [Deployment]
   validate:
     message: "Deployment must have otel.instrumentation=enabled annotation"
     anyPattern:
     - metadata:
         annotations:
           otel.instrumentation: "enabled"
 - name: require-otel-configuration
   match:
     resources:
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Question Is Asked

This question evaluates your ability to govern multi-tenant Kubernetes clusters using policy-as-code tooling. It tests your understanding of enforceable, testable guardrails that operate at CI time, combining practical knowledge of Kyverno and OPA, QoS classes, namespace quotas, and HPA configuration with real manifest examples and end-to-end verification workflows.

## Key Concepts

### Pod Resource Requirements
Kubernetes uses requests and limits to manage resource allocation. Requests define guaranteed resources; limits cap maximum usage. Without these, the scheduler cannot make informed placement decisions, and noisy neighbor issues arise in multi-tenant environments.

### QoS Classes
Kubernetes assigns three QoS classes based on resource configuration:
- **Guaranteed**: All containers must set both requests and limits, and they must be equal
- **Burstable**: Containers have requests but limits differ from requests (or limits are absent)
- **BestEffort**: Containers have no resource requests or limits

The Burstable QoS rule demonstrates namespace-tiered policy—premium tenants may need bursty workloads while standard tenants require predictable resource behavior.

### Hard Resource Caps
Namespace-level quotas prevent a single tenant from exhausting cluster capacity. Gatekeeper constraints evaluate aggregated resource requests across all pods in a namespace, not just individual pod specs.

### HPA Baseline Utilization
HPAs require meaningful target utilization (typically 50-90%) to function effectively. Without this, autoscaling either triggers too aggressively or not at all, undermining cost optimization.

## Design Rationale

| Policy | Tool | Rationale |
|--------|------|-----------|
| Resource requirements | Kyverno | Native pattern matching simplifies container spec validation |
| Burstable QoS | Kyverno | Preconditions enable namespace label checks |
| Namespace quota | Gatekeeper | Rego can aggregate data across pods within a namespace |
| HPA metrics | Kyverno | AnyPattern allows multiple valid metric configurations |

## Common Pitfalls

1. **Background policy conflicts**: Setting `background: false` prevents automatic scanning of existing resources—use carefully
2. **Rego data access**: Gatekeeper constraint templates require proper inventory lookups to aggregate namespace-wide data
3. **CI timing**: Policy enforcement happens at admission time; CI gates validate manifests before they reach the cluster

## Why This Is Asked

In production Kubernetes environments, ensuring supply-chain security for Helm-based deployments is critical. This question evaluates your ability to integrate multiple security tools—Helm templating, SBOM generation, and image signature verification—into a cohesive CI gate. It tests practical knowledge of enforcing provenance and attestations before code merges.

## Key Concepts

- **Helm templating and values extraction**: Rendering charts to discover all container images referenced in deployments
- **SBOM generation**: Using Syft to create a CycloneDX SBOM that catalogs all dependencies and artifacts
- **Image signing verification**: Using cosign to validate container image signatures against a public key stored in the repository
- **CI gate integration**: Implementing fail-fast behavior in GitHub Actions to block unsigned images and missing attestations

## Code Example

```yaml
# Minimal GitHub Actions workflow for Helm image signing enforcement
name: Helm Image Security Gate

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  helm-security:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3

      - name: Install Helm and Syft
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/helm/helm/main/scripts/get-helm-3 | bash
          curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anchore/syft/main/install.sh | sh

      - name: Render Helm templates
        run: helm template my-app ./chart --values values.yaml --output-dir ./rendered

      - name: Extract image references
        run: |
          grep -rh 'image:' ./rendered | awk '{print $2}' > images.txt

      - name: Generate SBOM with Syft
        run: |
          syft $(cat images.txt) -o cyclonedx-json > sbom.json

      - name: Verify image signatures with cosign
        run: |
          COSIGN_PUBLIC_KEY=cosign.pub
          for IMAGE in $(cat images.txt); do
            cosign verify --key $COSIGN_PUBLIC_KEY $IMAGE || exit 1
          done
```

```yaml
name: Security gate
on: [push]
jobs:

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

        uses: docker/build-push-action@v4

          tags: myservice:latest
      - name: Trivy image
        uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@v2
```

## Why This Is Asked

Tests practical ability to implement cross-cluster identity-based API security, not just resource-level controls.

- SPIFFE/SPIRE identities
- mTLS for API surface
- OPA/rego identity-based access
- Cross-cluster policy enforcement

## Code Example

```javascript
// Pseudo-rego policy example for demonstration
const policy = `package kubesecr.identity
default allow = false
allow {
  input.subject == 'spiffe://cluster/example/ns/production/sa/api-server'
  input.path == '/api/v1'
  input.method == 'GET'
}`
export default policy;
```
